answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation with slow trust accrual: a new agent posts a small refundable bond and completes low-value, verifiable tasks before handling larger trades, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets becomes costly rather than free. Like stars emerging from a nebula, legitimate reputations form gradually from a diffuse cloud of small interactions, while an umber stain of failed deliveries marks bad actors and follows the identity. A sybil swarm hits its nadir when bonded identities are slashed faster than it can profitably replace them.
